work_atc.config.air_traffic_controller_s: Air traffic controller (San Andreas Control, San Fierro)
work_atc.trn.acc.airspace_intro: Radar sees every aircraft of the FIR, and refreshes every 3 seconds. Your aircraft are the ones in the CTA; in the TMAs and CTRs approach and the towers work (all closed in this training).
work_atc.trn.acc.airspace_sectors: The CTA can be split between more controllers: north / south (the line ZEPHR - PALIS - VINEW - east edge), and lower / upper at FL205 (SACC_N, S, U, NU, SU). An aircraft belongs to the first open position of its sector; {position} alone has all of them. AT shows the airspace names.
work_atc.trn.acc.alerts_fines: Separation losses in your sector are fined: in the CTA {cta}, in a TMA {tma}. Overflights over a TMA stay at 6000 ft or higher (LOA); below that they are coordinated with approach.
work_atc.trn.acc.alerts_list: Label alerts (red): EMRG = 7700 emergency, COMS = 7600 radio failure, DUPE = two aircraft with the same squawk, STCA = separation loss, RAM = it left its route for a long time (check your headings).
work_atc.trn.acc.alerts_logout: Press Logout in the top right corner. Nothing is paid in the training, you only see the receipt.
work_atc.trn.acc.alerts_pay: Pay: {per_action} per accepted command, +{bonus}% per minute (at most x{max}), {per_aircraft} per aircraft. With radar you have every ATC position: tower, approach and San Andreas Control.
work_atc.trn.acc.cf_spot:
Watch out: {cfa} and {cfb} fly head-on on the same route at the same level ({level}). Minimum separation in the CTA: 0.1 nm or 1000 ft. A loss is STCA (red) and a fine.

Separate them now: give one of them a level at least 1000 ft higher or lower (Cleared altitude), or turn one away with a heading.
work_atc.trn.acc.cf_watch: Good. A climb or a descent takes time (about 2000 ft per minute), so act early. Watch them pass each other. If you turned one, send it back with Direct to or Resume own navigation afterwards.
work_atc.trn.acc.console_login:
Log in as {position}: San Andreas Control, the whole CTA - the airspace outside the TMAs, and everything above them.

Click Log in.
work_atc.trn.acc.console_walk: Radar (San Andreas Control) is opened at the ACC console in front of the wall screens. Walk into its blue marker and press {console}.
work_atc.trn.acc.done_text:
In short:
1. Overflights: their level, Direct to for a shorter route.
2. Conflicts: 1000 ft or 0.1 nm, act early (levels take time).
3. Arrivals: 4000 ft or lower at the TMA entry fix, arrival procedure, transfer to approach.
4. Departures from approach come at 5000 ft: climb them to their RFL.

Read OPS-4 (area) and the LOA on sanandreascontrol.eu.
work_atc.trn.acc.inb_descend: {inb} is yours. LOA: arrivals reach the TMA entry fix at 4000 ft or lower (3000 ft on the short STARs). Descend it now: Cleared altitude > 4000. Big descents take long, start early.
work_atc.trn.acc.inb_leave: At the entry fix {inb} enters the TMA and belongs to approach. Live you transfer it before the entry fix (Transfer to); approach is closed now, so it flies on alone.
work_atc.trn.acc.inb_star: Radar may also give the arrival procedure: Arrival procedure > the suggested STAR (yellow) for runway {arr_rwy}. Then approach gets it ready.
work_atc.trn.acc.inb_wait: An arrival to {airport} ({inb}) enters the CTA.
work_atc.trn.acc.ovf_direct: Shorten its route: Direct to > a fix further along its route. The flight plan continues after that fix.
work_atc.trn.acc.ovf_leave: {ovf} leaves the CTA at a border fix and disappears from your radar.
work_atc.trn.acc.ovf_level: {ovf} is yours. Overflights fly their requested level (RFL). Give it a new level: Cleared altitude > for example 2000 ft higher.
work_atc.trn.acc.ovf_wait: An overflight ({ovf}) is about to enter the CTA. Outside the border it is nobody's, its label is grey.
work_atc.trn.adc.air_leave: Your sector is the CTR of {airport}: the ground, the runway and a strip of air around it. The tower does not give a departure levels or headings: it got its initial level with the IFR clearance, and only approach (APP) climbs it further. When {dep} leaves the CTR, it belongs to approach; approach is closed now, so the pilots fly their flight plan alone and the label turns grey.
work_atc.trn.adc.air_wait: {dep} is rolling. After take-off it flies the runway heading up to 800 ft above the field, then its SID, and climbs to the initial level.
work_atc.trn.adc.alerts_emrg: The red EMRG above the label is an alert: {arr} squawks 7700, an emergency. Others: COMS = 7600 radio failure, DUPE = two aircraft with the same squawk, STCA = separation loss, RAM = the aircraft left its route.
work_atc.trn.adc.alerts_fines: Separation losses are fined, but only in your own sector: two ground aircraft head-on {gnd}; closer than 0.1 nm and 1000 ft in a TMA {tma}, in the CTA {cta}. Fines are taken from your pay, even when the total is negative.
work_atc.trn.adc.alerts_logout: Press Logout in the top right corner. In the training nothing is paid, you only see the receipt.
work_atc.trn.adc.alerts_pay:
You are paid when you log out: {per_action} for every accepted command, more the longer you stay (+{bonus}% per minute, at most x{max}), and {per_aircraft} for every aircraft you controlled. Every command also gives work XP.

You start as a tower controller; approach (APP) comes at level {app}, radar (centre) at level {radar}.
work_atc.trn.adc.arr_land: {arr} comes from approach (APP), already cleared for the approach: it flies to the final fix and on to the runway. Its label is grey until it reaches your CTR / the final; then it is yours and asks for the landing clearance (LAND, yellow). Give Cleared to land before it is 400 m from the threshold, otherwise it goes around.
work_atc.trn.adc.arr_parked: {arr} taxies to the stand. Wait until it parks.
work_atc.trn.adc.arr_taxi: {arr} has landed. Off the runway it asks for taxi: Taxi to stand > any free stand, or a named one.
work_atc.trn.adc.arr_vacate:
With Vacate via > you can name the runway exit; without it the pilots take the first one towards the terminal. Go around sends it round again if the runway is not free.

Wait for the landing.
work_atc.trn.adc.arr_wait: An arrival ({arr}) is coming on the final of runway {arr_rwy}...
work_atc.trn.adc.console_login:
The login window lists the positions of this console. You start as a tower controller ({position}): the tower controls the aircraft on the ground, on the runway and in the CTR around the airport.

Click Log in.
work_atc.trn.adc.console_walk:
The tower of {airport} is opened at the {airport} consoles of the operations room.

Walk into the blue marker of the {airport} consoles and press {console}.
work_atc.trn.adc.delivery_ifr: First the IFR clearance: in the menu choose IFR clearance >, then the departure procedure (SID). The yellow one is suggested: it starts the filed route from the runway in use. Then the initial level: 3000 ft is the standard.
work_atc.trn.adc.delivery_push: Cleared! The label now asks for PUSH. Open the menu again and choose Pushback approved.
work_atc.trn.adc.delivery_pushing: {dep} is pushed back tail first onto the taxiway, nose towards the runway. When it stops, it asks for taxi (TAXI).
work_atc.trn.adc.done_text:
In short:
1. Go on duty, then the console in the SA Control room: {console}, Log in.
2. Departures: IFR clearance, Pushback, Taxi, Take-off; leaving the CTR they go to approach.
3. Arrivals (from approach): Cleared to land, Taxi to stand.
4. Yellow = they ask, red = alert. Watch the separation.
5. Logout pays.

Read the documents on sanandreascontrol.eu (in-game browser): NAV, SW, OPS, then LOA. At work level {app} the APC (approach) module opens at the training marker.
work_atc.trn.adc.ground_rules:
While taxiing: aircraft keep 60 m behind each other in a queue, and nobody enters a runway without your clearance: they stop before it (holding short) and ask.

Two aircraft facing each other on a taxiway is a separation loss (a fine) - plan the taxi routes.
work_atc.trn.adc.ground_takeoff:
It holds short and asks (yellow in the menu): CROSS = Cross runway; BKTRK = Backtrack runway (it rolls to the threshold on the runway and turns round); T/O = Line up and wait or Cleared for take-off. Take-off clearance is accepted only at the runway.

Clear {dep} for take-off.
work_atc.trn.adc.ground_taxi: Choose Taxi > and the runway: the one in use ({dep_rwy}) is marked. The pilots find the way on the taxiways by themselves.
work_atc.trn.adc.label_menu: {dep} is at its stand and asks for its IFR clearance (yellow frame). Open its menu.
work_atc.trn.adc.label_menu_info: On the ground the menu lists the whole flow of a departure in order: IFR clearance, Pushback, Taxi, then the runway. Only the step it is at now can be clicked, the rest is grey.
work_atc.trn.adc.label_wait: A departure ({dep}) is coming to a stand of {airport}...
work_atc.trn.apc.airspace_fixes: Turn on AT and FIXL. The fixes on the TMA boundary are the doors of your airspace: arrival procedures (STAR, e.g. MISTY1A) start at them, departure procedures (SID, e.g. MISTY1D) end at them.
work_atc.trn.apc.airspace_intro:
Your sector is the TMA of {airport}, up to 5500 ft, without the CTR. You see the traffic of your airport up to 7500 ft, and everything that crosses your TMA. The approach radar refreshes every 2 seconds, so the targets jump.

Tower and radar (San Andreas Control) are closed in this training: outside your TMA the pilots fly on their own.
work_atc.trn.apc.airspace_runways: The runways in use (now landing {arr_rwy}, take-off {dep_rwy}) decide where your arrivals go: every arrival procedure ends at the final fix of a runway.
work_atc.trn.apc.alerts_logout: Press Logout in the top right corner. Nothing is paid in the training, you only see the receipt.
work_atc.trn.apc.alerts_pay: Pay works as for the tower: {per_action} per accepted command, +{bonus}% per minute (at most x{max}), {per_aircraft} per aircraft. Radar (centre) and the ACC training module open at work level {radar}.
work_atc.trn.apc.alerts_rules:
The rules of approach (LOA): arrivals come from radar at 4000 ft or lower at the entry fix, you give them to the tower cleared for the approach at 1500 ft. Departures get 5000 ft by the exit fix. Overflights cross the TMA at 6000 ft or higher and stay with radar. A go-around climbs to 3000 ft and is yours again.

Separation in the TMA: 0.1 nm or 1000 ft; a loss in your sector costs {tma}.
work_atc.trn.apc.arr_approach: Close to the final fix it asks for the approach clearance (APP, yellow). Give Cleared approach: without it, it flies on past the final fix on its heading and you have to vector it back.
work_atc.trn.apc.arr_descend: {arr} is in your TMA: it is yours, on its STAR (in the waypoint field of the label; Arrival procedure > would change it or the runway). Descend it: Cleared altitude > 1500 ft. At the final fix it must be at most 1700 ft above the field, otherwise it goes around. The STARs are short, so descend at once.
work_atc.trn.apc.arr_leave: On the final it belongs to the tower. The tower is closed now, so the pilots land on their own. Live you transfer it to the tower no later than the final fix, cleared for the approach, at 1500 ft (LOA).
work_atc.trn.apc.arr_wait: An arrival ({arr}) comes from San Andreas Control towards the entry fix {arr_entry} at 4000 ft. In the CTA it belongs to radar (closed now), so the label is grey, and the pilots picked the arrival procedure (STAR) of their entry fix themselves.
work_atc.trn.apc.console_login:
Log in as approach ({position}). Approach controls the airborne traffic in the TMA of {airport} - except the CTR in its middle, which belongs to the tower.

Click Log in.
work_atc.trn.apc.console_walk: Approach is opened at the same console as the tower. Walk into the blue marker of the {airport} consoles and press {console}.
work_atc.trn.apc.dep_climb: {dep} is in your TMA: its label is white, it is yours. Departures leave the TMA at 5000 ft (LOA). Click its label: Cleared altitude > 5000.
work_atc.trn.apc.dep_direct: You may shorten the route: Direct to > the exit fix of its SID (it is in the label's waypoint field and in the route). Or turn it with Fly heading. Give it one of them.
work_atc.trn.apc.dep_leave: At the exit fix {dep} leaves your TMA and belongs to radar. Live you transfer it before the boundary (Transfer to > SACC); radar is closed now, so it flies on alone.
work_atc.trn.apc.dep_wait: A departure ({dep}) leaves a stand of {airport}. The tower is closed, so the pilots push back, taxi and take off on their own and fly their SID. Its label is grey until it climbs out of the CTR into your TMA.
work_atc.trn.apc.done_text:
In short:
1. Departures: Cleared altitude 5000, Direct to / heading, transfer before the exit fix.
2. Arrivals: on a STAR (Arrival procedure changes it), Cleared altitude 1500, Cleared approach, transfer to the tower by the final fix.
3. Vectors: a heading at most 30 deg to the centre line, then Cleared approach.

Read OPS-3 (approach) and the LOA on sanandreascontrol.eu.
work_atc.trn.apc.vec_approach: When the heading meets the centre line (it asks for APP), give Cleared approach: it keeps the heading and turns onto the final by itself. With a bad heading, the clearance sends it direct to the nearest final fix instead. Correct the heading any time.
work_atc.trn.apc.vec_descend: Descend it as well: Cleared altitude > 1500 ft.
work_atc.trn.apc.vec_heading: {vec} is yours. It has no STAR, and it asks for the approach clearance at once - first vector it. Click its label: Fly heading > (or Turn left / right heading). Pick the heading on the compass ring around it (mouse wheel = 5 deg), so that it meets the extended centre line of runway {arr_rwy} at most 30 deg off, before the final fix. The cyan line shows the turn.
work_atc.trn.apc.vec_leave: Established on the final it goes to the tower and lands.
work_atc.trn.apc.vec_wait: Another arrival ({vec}) towards {vec_entry}. This time you do not give a STAR: you vector it with headings.
work_atc.trn.card.click_again_to_skip: Click again to quit the training module
work_atc.trn.card.title: Air traffic control training
work_atc.trn.common.note_fast: Fast forward x{scale}: nobody is waiting for you.
work_atc.trn.common.note_go_around: It went around: it flies the go-around procedure (GA) up to 3000 ft and comes back for a new approach. Clear it again.
work_atc.trn.common.note_open_console: Stand in the console marker and press {console}.
work_atc.trn.common.note_open_scope: The scope is hidden: press {console} at the console marker.
work_atc.trn.common.offer:
Welcome to San Andreas Control! Would you like a short tour of the radar scope now? It shows where everything is on the scope and the menu you give the commands in. It takes about {minutes} minutes, and you can stop it any time.

The modules (SCOPE, then ADC, APC, ACC) are at the training marker in the SA Control room.
work_atc.trn.common.title: {code} training
work_atc.trn.menu.acc_desc: Radar: the CTA, overflights, a conflict and the handover to approach. About {minutes} min.
work_atc.trn.menu.adc_desc: Tower: delivery, ground, runway and the CTR. About {minutes} min.
work_atc.trn.menu.apc_desc: Approach: departures and arrivals in the TMA, STARs and radar vectors. About {minutes} min.
work_atc.trn.menu.scope_desc: Where everything is on the scope, labels and the command menu. Start here. About {minutes} min.
work_atc.trn.menu.text: SCOPE shows the radar scope itself; the other three teach one controller position each and take the scope as known. A module opens with the right of its position (your work level). Your live position stays free while you train, and nothing is paid.
work_atc.trn.menu.title: ATC training
work_atc.trn.scope.console_login:
The login window lists the positions of this console. You log in as the tower ({position}): the scope looks the same at every position.

Click Log in.
work_atc.trn.scope.console_walk:
You are in the operations room of San Andreas Control. Every ATC position is opened here; the airport towers have no consoles.

Walk into the blue marker of the {airport} consoles and press {console}.
work_atc.trn.scope.done_text:
In short:
1. Console in the SA Control room: {console}, Log in.
2. Top bar: runways and wind. AT / FIXL / V- V+, wheel = zoom, right button = move.
3. Lists on the right; yellow REQ = it asks you.
4. Click a label: the command menu.
5. Logout pays.

Next: the ADC (tower) module at the training marker.
work_atc.trn.scope.logout: Press Logout in the top right corner. In the training nothing is paid, you only see the receipt.
work_atc.trn.scope.menu_info: At the top is the flight: type, route, procedure, who controls it. Below are the commands in groups; yellow = what the pilots ask for, grey = not possible now. The position modules teach which ones to give.
work_atc.trn.scope.menu_label: Every aircraft has a label: the callsign first, then its data (on the ground speed and squawk, in the air altitude in hundreds of feet, speed, destination). A yellow frame means it asks you for something, a grey label is not yours. You can drag a label with the left mouse button.
work_atc.trn.scope.menu_open: You give every command in the menu of the aircraft. Click the label of {dep}.
work_atc.trn.scope.menu_wait: A departure ({dep}) is coming to a stand of {airport}...
work_atc.trn.scope.tour_buttons: List: on/off hides the lists, Reset view brings the map back. Hide closes the scope but you stay logged in ({console} at the console shows it again). Logout ends the session and pays you.
work_atc.trn.scope.tour_intro: This is the radar scope. You look at the airspace from above: the CTR of {airport} around the runways, the TMA around it, the fixes (triangles), and the aircraft with their labels.
work_atc.trn.scope.tour_list: On the right are the lists of your traffic. Your aircraft are blue; a yellow REQ means it asks you for something. Clicking a row centres the map on it.
work_atc.trn.scope.tour_tools: AT shows / hides the airspace names, FIXL the fix names. V- / V+ (or the keys 0-5) set the length of the speed vector ahead of the airborne aircraft.
work_atc.trn.scope.tour_topbar: The top bar: your position, the runways in use (ARR = landing, DEP = take-off, now {arr_rwy} / {dep_rwy}) and the wind.
work_atc.trn.scope.tour_view: Mouse wheel: zoom where the cursor is. Right mouse button held: move the map. Taxiways, stands and ground traffic appear only when you zoom in. Distances are in nautical miles (scale bar), altitudes in feet, speeds in knots.
work_atc.trn.server.aircraft_failed: The training aircraft could not be created, the module ends.
work_atc.trn.server.aircraft_lost: A training aircraft was removed, a new one comes.
work_atc.trn.server.already_running: A training module is already running.
work_atc.trn.server.cannot_start_now: You cannot start a training module now.
work_atc.trn.server.completed: {code} training completed. Have a good shift!
work_atc.trn.server.could_not_start: The training module could not be started.
work_atc.trn.server.duty_first: Go on duty as an air traffic controller first.
work_atc.trn.server.ended_died: The training ended because you died.
work_atc.trn.server.locked: The {code} module is locked: it opens with the right of that position (work level {level}).
work_atc.trn.server.log_out_first: Log out of your ATC position first.
work_atc.trn.server.logged_out_early: You logged out before the end. Log in again at the console ({console}).
work_atc.trn.server.no_problem: No problem. The training modules are at the training marker in the SA Control room.
work_atc.trn.server.quit: {code} training stopped. You can start it again at the training marker in the SA Control room.
work_atc.trn.server.system_not_running: The air traffic control system is not running, the training cannot go on.
work_atc.trn.server.usage: The training modules start at the training marker in the SA Control room. /{command} stop ends the running one.
